findings.text: follow-on: the retry is unbounded. The resume branch (recovery.py:2270) runs on every sweep for an unpromoted finding-bearing run whose worker is not live; the only thing that ends it is the reviewed run's head moving past the reviewed head (after a commit, _stored_review returns None and the round is dropped). A resumed turn that ends without moving the head therefore resumes again on the next sweep, and again after that, forever: the attempt count at recovery.py:2294 is recorded but never read as a cap, and _repair_launch_refusal (recovery.py:1959) has no attempt limit. The node brief's done_when reads 'a second sweep for the same round resumes nothing', which the finished-turn case at tests/test_the_reflex_resumes_an_unpromoted_run.py:305 contradicts by design (it asserts a second sweep resumes, attempt 2). This is the same cadence-churn class the s3 guards were raised against (a round re-firing every cadence), bounded here only by the reviewed run eventually committing.

follow-on: changed_paths under-reports the diff. It names four paths (reckon/crew/recovery.py, tests/test_the_reflex_resumes_an_unpromoted_run.py, tests/test_repair_answers_only_blocking_findings.py, the evidence fragment), but the diff base..head edits three further files outside the declared fence: tests/test_a_repair_hold_names_its_cause.py, tests/test_reflex_dispatches_one_repair.py and tests/test_repair_skips_out_of_repo_foundings.py, all in commit 58d5e62c3 ('align the reflex tests'). Those three are a fence breach (the fence is recovery.py, the new test and the evidence fragment) and are not named in changed_paths, so the record does not disclose what the diff shows. The edits are visible in git and were disclosed in the earlier review's record, but the run's own manifest should name every path it changed.

follow-on: test_a_promoted_reviewed_run_is_not_resumed asserts only recorded.get('status') != 'resumed' (line 376), which passes whether the recorded repair_dispatch carries status 'refused', some other value, or is absent entirely, so it does not pin the promoted-run refusal it names. It should assert the recorded status is exactly the refusal the promoted path writes (the dispatch path is taken and its launch refusal is what settles it).

follow-on: the 'attempt' returned to the caller (recovery.py:2294) is computed from the entry-time record mapping, while the durable attempt is incremented independently inside _record_repair_dispatch (recovery.py:1878) from a fresh pointer read. The two can disagree whenever the pointer moved between the function's entry read and the write, so the returned report's attempt is not the recorded one. The stored pointer value is authoritative; a caller trusting the report would read a stale count.

follow-on: the node's declared negative_control (from its brief) was 'route the unpromoted case back to dispatch_module.dispatch; the resumed-not-dispatched case must fail', but the control actually run (negative-control-any-assistant-record-busy.log) restores the any-assistant-record busy check instead. That control is legitimate and does fire (1 failed, EXIT=1), but the brief's named falsification of the central resume-vs-dispatch decision was not exercised; the central decision rests on the gate test alone (test_an_unpromoted_exited_run_is_resumed_not_dispatched asserts dispatched == []).
